finding.claim: Caller identity is taken from the client-supplied X-Session-User-Verified header with no verification, so any HTTP client can impersonate any user and pass the ACL checks on delete and rename (conditional on the app being reachable without a proxy that overwrites that header).
finding.source: views.py:11 request.headers.get("X-Session-User-Verified") in before_request load_user; attacker controls the header value.
finding.sink: views.py:17 ensure_allowed(g.user, f, "delete") -> DELETE /files/<fid> and views.py:25 is_allowed(g.user, f, "write") -> POST /files/<fid>/rename (acl.py:5 grants lookup keyed by user).

trace.note: g.user set directly from request header; no signature, session, or proxy-origin check
delete_file uses g.user for ACL check
is_allowed looks up resource['grants'][user] and checks action membership; trusts whatever user string is passed
ensure_allowed aborts 403 only when is_allowed is False; impersonated user with a grant passes
file is deleted for the impersonated user
rename path has the same identity source and check

finding.guards_checked: Per-object ACL check on the same object acted upon (correct: f from STORE[fid] is both checked and modified). Action names are distinct (delete vs write). No mass assignment: rename only writes f['name'] from request.json['name']. Grants are not writable through any route. No auth middleware other than load_user exists in this file. Could not verify upstream proxy behaviour from this repo; if a trusted gateway strips and re-sets the header on every request, severity drops to none. Missing-id requests raise KeyError (500) while unauthorized existing ids return 403; this is a minor id-existence oracle and is not reported as a finding.

verdict.guard_found: none in the repo. views.py:11 takes the identity straight from the request header, and acl.py:5 and acl.py:9-10 (abort at :10) trust whatever user string they receive. The only other candidate control is an upstream proxy that strips and re-sets X-Session-User-Verified, and the repo (Glob shows only acl.py and views.py) contains no such proxy or config.
verdict.reason: The code path is real and nothing in views.py:11 or acl.py:5-10 verifies the header, so the flaw is confirmed if the app is reachable without a proxy that overwrites the header, but that deployment fact is not in the repo, so I cannot decide reachability from the code alone. Minor trace note: the candidate cites acl.py:8 for the abort, but that is the def line; the abort is at acl.py:10.
